description: FIRST SWEEP GOLDEN (the first NON-PRISMATIC feature): an r=8 mm circular profile on the XY datum plane swept along a straight 30 mm OPEN path (a second sketch, a vertical line on the XZ datum plane) into a right circular cylinder along +Z. A THREE-feature TREE (profile sketch -> path sketch -> sweep) evaluated through the same evaluate-tree path as the extrude/revolve goldens: planegcs solves BOTH sketches -> the profile wire assembles + closes (SHARED build_profile_face) while the path assembles into a single OPEN wire (build_path_wire, the open-wire sibling sharing the same per-entity edge builder) -> Solid.sweep along the path (anchored at the profile) -> add against the (empty) body -> GProp -> tessellation -> content-addressed GLB. Locks: the sweep handler + the path-sketch FeatureRef resolution (option A, the second sketch reference slot) + open-wire assembly + Solid.sweep of a circle along a straight path, GProp over one cylindrical surface + two caps, curved-face tessellation of the periodic (seamed) cylinder, and (via the parametrized round-trip gate) STEP re-approximation of the swept cylindrical surface. A right cylinder is the analytic anchor the brief calls for (volume pi*r^2*L): the swept solid is topologically the canonical cylinder, so this doubles as a cross-check that Solid.sweep reproduces build_cylinder's B-rep exactly by an entirely different code path.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). The profile is a full circle of radius r=8 mm centred at the origin on the XY datum plane (normal +Z). The path is a straight OPEN line of length L=30 mm along +Z, drawn on the XZ datum plane as a vertical sketch line from (0,0) to (0,30) — on XZ, sketch (x,y) maps to world (x,0,y), so (0,0)->(0,0,0) and (0,30)->(0,0,30), i.e. a segment straight up +Z. The path's first (only) segment is perpendicular to the profile plane and starts at the profile origin: the ideal, well-posed sweep. Sweeping the circle along it yields a right circular cylinder, base disc at z=0, axis +Z, height L.

Both sketches are FULLY constrained at their analytic solution with zero residual (status converged, 0 DOF): the circle by a fixed centre (at the origin) + radius=8; the path line by a fixed start (at the origin) + vertical + distance=30 (start fixed, end pinned to (0,30) by vertical+length, matching where it was drawn). Because the start position is already the solution, planegcs provably returns the input positions bitwise — verified 2026-07-12 (solved == input on both sketches). No solver error is introduced.
volume = pi*r^2*L = pi*8^2*30 = pi*1920 = 6031.857894892402 mm^3 (nearest double to 1920*pi).
surface_area = 2*pi*r*(r + L) = 2*pi*8*(8 + 30) = 2*pi*8*38 = 608*pi = 1910.088333382594 mm^2 (lateral 2*pi*r*L = 480*pi plus two caps 2 * pi*r^2 = 128*pi).
centroid = (0, 0, L/2) = (0, 0, 15) mm by symmetry: the axis passes through the origin along +Z. (GProp puts x,y at ulp scale ~1e-15, z exactly 15 to one ulp.)

bounding_box = [-r,-r,0]..[r,r,L] = [-8,-8,0]..[8,8,30]: the base disc is centred at the origin (path anchored at the profile) and the sweep runs the full L up +Z; the optimal (exact) AABB of a Z-axis cylinder is the square prism of half-width r.

topology: OCCT models the closed swept cylinder identically to a built cylinder — 3 faces (1 cylindrical lateral + 2 planar caps), 3 edges (2 cap circles + 1 straight SEAM edge where the periodic cylindrical surface's parametrization closes), 1 closed shell. Vertices = 2 (the two endpoints of the seam edge).

mesh (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, isRelative=False): the circular boundary discretizes to 126 segments (angular-dominated: 2*ceil(2*pi/0.1)=126, the same rule the cylinder and revolve goldens exhibit; radius r=8 does not raise the linear estimate above this). Lateral = 2 rows * 127 nodes (127 = 126 segments + 1, the seam column duplicated in the parametric unwrap) = 254 nodes, 126*2 = 252 triangles. Each cap triangulates its 126-gon boundary with no interior vertex = 126 nodes, 126-2 = 124 triangles. Two caps -> 252 nodes / 248 triangles.

mesh totals = 254 + 252 = 506 vertices and 252 + 248 = 500 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing across faces — same convention as the box, cylinder, revolve, and fillet goldens). Identical to the cylinder-r10-h25 golden (both are the canonical seamed cylinder at this deflection), which is the intended cross-check: Solid.sweep reproduces the same B-rep + mesh as build_cylinder.

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned here: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CURVED-GEOMETRY tolerance, measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). The swept cylindrical surface goes through OCCT's Gauss-quadrature surface/volume integration in GProp — converging to machine precision but not exact zero. Measured deviations vs the analytic values (2026-07-12, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume 0.0 mm^3, surface_area 0.0 mm^2, centroid <= 1.44e-15 mm (x/y on the axis; z exactly 15 to one ulp, i.e. 14.999999999999998), AABB exactly 0.0 on all six bounds. Documented ceiling 1e-9 = ~7e5x the observed worst case (1.44e-15), headroom for libm/platform variation in the quadrature's transcendental evaluations across CI hosts — while staying 100x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 bound, matching the cylinder/revolve/fillet goldens' curved posture. The solver contributes zero error by construction (zero-residual start, solved == input bitwise). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
